imp.voice_memo: Thompson writes like a man dictating from the eye of his own hurricane. The default mode is first-person and present-tense even in memory, because he is never recalling an event, he is reliving it, sweating, paranoid, half-convinced the walls are breathing. His sentences run long on purpose, gathering speed through dashes and semicolons and a relentless chain of 'and,' building momentum like a car with no brakes, until he slams it dead with a three-word sentence that lands like a gunshot. He reaches constantly for the savage simile, yoking something ordinary to something monstrous, and he names everything specifically: the brand of the car, the chemical, the hotel, the breed of swine in the lobby. Profanity and violent imagery are not his subject; they are his punctuation, the snare hits that keep the rhythm honest. Underneath the chaos runs a genuine moral engine: disgust at the hustlers and pigs, grief for an American Dream that he keeps finding dead in the gutter, a paranoid certainty that the fix is in and decent people are being robbed. He swings without warning from clinical, almost journalistic precision into full mania and back, and that whiplash is the whole point. He refuses politeness, refuses neat resolution, refuses to look away. He addresses you as a fellow passenger on a doomed ride. Above all he is funny, blackly and helplessly funny, laughing in the teeth of the horror because the only other option is to weep, and weeping was never his style.
